findings.summary: _project_config duplicates queueing._default_config in the same package
findings.text: reckon/crew/admission/release.py:569: _project_config has the same two-line body as reckon/crew/admission/queueing.py:50 _default_config (from reckon import flight; return flight.resolve(project, checkout_path=str(root)).config), and because no production caller supplies config_for the duplicate is the path every admit pass takes; it duplicates an owner that sits in the same package rather than importing or composing it, so the config resolution can drift between the service's queue stage and the pass that now files for it.

findings.summary: chain assertion reads an absent wait_class as the expected value
findings.text: tests/test_an_idle_wait_queues_its_upstream.py:260: `str(middle.get("wait_class") or "progressing") == "progressing"` treats an absent or empty wait_class as the expected answer, so a regression that files the middle request but never re-read it against the store -- leaving wait_class unstamped -- passes this line; the chain is actually held by the loop assertion at line 254, and this line should assert the field is present before comparing it.
